Leah Park: Quick preflight: planning to enable feature flag `routing_v2` for a 5% canary on route /search next week. Project default is OFF. Can we confirm how precedence works when route+project+model differ? Who owns rollback guardrails?
Evan Cho: Route > Project > Org by default. Model-level flags are applied after route resolution for model-specific overrides (model only if explicitly set).
Carla Mendez: Correct. Also note we have an emergency 'force_disable' at org that trumps everything.
Samir Patel: Ops note: our rollout service evaluates in this order: route -> model -> project -> org, but any "force_*" keys are checked first. Might be surprising.
Leah Park: Ugh, that order is scary. Can we get a quick example?
Evan Cho: Example config snippet:
```
org: {force_disable: false}
project: {routing_v2: false}
route: {routing_v2: {enabled: true, canary: 0.05}}
model: {routing_v2: {enabled: true}}
```
Resolution -> route enabled for 5% because route explicit. If org.force_disable true -> everything off.
Carla Mendez: Also remember audience-level canary is evaluated after scope resolution. So route-level canary will only target the traffic for that route.
Leah Park: Good. Who will own the rollout monitor and auto-rollback thresholds? I can set up the monitor but need someone to own auto-rollback policy.
Samir Patel: I'll own the auto-rollback policy for this canary. Suggest thresholds: error_rate > 1% for 5m or latency p95 +50% over baseline.
Carla Mendez: Works for me. @Evan can you add a quick check to the flag linting to warn if project=false and route=true without an explicit owner tag? :eyes:
Evan Cho: Yep, will add a lint rule and a one-off alert.

ops-bot: deploy-prod started for service search-router (rev: b7f9d2)
Leah Park: Thanks all. I'll open PR referencing this thread, add the canary monitor, tag @Carla and @Samir. Plan to flip to 100% only after 24h stable. :thumbsup:
